note: Syllabus tracker. Each topic is listed once and linked to every GATE and NET section it belongs to. Questions are linked to topics by writer first (writers, plus alsoWriters for a writer's secondary topic), then by tags (each rule is a list that must all match; 'sec:X' = paper section, '!Tag' = must not have), then by the Guide topic. Each question gets one home topic (counted once) and may also be listed in a few others for quizzing.

sections.name: Verbal Aptitude
sections.about: Basic English grammar, vocabulary, idioms and phrases in context; reading and comprehension; narrative sequencing.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.about: Data interpretation (graphs, charts, plots, maps, tables); ratios, percentages, powers, logarithms, permutations and combinations, series; mensuration, geometry, elementary statistics and probability.

sections.name: Analytical Aptitude
sections.about: Logic: deduction and induction; analogy; numerical relations and reasoning.

sections.name: Spatial Aptitude
sections.about: Transforming shapes: translation, rotation, scaling, mirroring, assembling and grouping; paper folding, cutting and patterns in 2D and 3D.

sections.name: Reading Comprehension
sections.about: Understanding complex language in short paragraphs and answering questions on them.

sections.name: Expression
sections.about: Stylistic and rhetorical aspects of a short passage, including correcting or modifying particular sentences.

sections.name: Analytical Reasoning
sections.about: Understanding relationships in statements or short passages and drawing reasonable conclusions from them.

sections.name: Logical Reasoning
sections.about: Thinking critically to evaluate or predict an argument, identify main and supporting arguments, and predict outcomes.

sections.name: Literary Forms, Genres and Modes of Expression
sections.about: Poetry, drama, fiction (novels, short stories, graphic narratives), creative non-fiction and non-fiction prose from the Medieval period to the present. Genres and subgenres: history, evolution and why categorisation matters. Aesthetic and rhetorical strategies: narrative and poetic techniques, figures of speech.

sections.name: History of English Literature and Literary Studies
sections.about: English literary traditions from Chaucer to the contemporary. Anglophone literatures: British, American, Canadian and other postcolonial literatures. Literature and political, social and intellectual movements. Literary studies and sociology, psychology, philosophy, environment and other allied disciplines.

sections.name: Comparative and World Literatures in English Translation
sections.about: Literatures in English translation, especially from India and the Global South. Cross-cultural exchanges. Comparative frameworks: intertextuality, adaptation, interconnectedness, cosmopolitanism. Multilingualism, translation studies and the politics of language.

sections.name: Critical Theories and Intellectual Traditions
sections.about: Structuralism, Marxism, Feminism, Existentialism, Poststructuralism, Modernism, Postmodernism, New Historicism, Postcolonialism, Posthumanism, etc. Cultural studies; film and media; memory and trauma; Dalit and Subaltern studies; environmental, medical and digital humanities. Indian poetics: Rasa, Dhvani, Vakrokti, Alamkara, Riti, Aucitya and other indigenous frameworks.

sections.name: Contemporary Literary Cultures and Research Methodologies
sections.about: Literary awards and prizes, festivals, associations and networks. Archival research, ethnographic methods, textual and discourse analysis, AI-assisted and multimodal approaches. Structuring arguments, academic integrity, plagiarism checking, citation ethics, engaging with scholarship.
